cells.note: No output.enforced cell: the documented behaviour is no fixed cap, with the ceiling being window minus prompt. That is a FUNCTION of the request, not a constant, and this schema has no shape for it — geometry plus window is what a consumer needs to derive it. Writing a number here would state a constant that does not exist. The catalog's output=500000 equals its context and is a placeholder by the spec's own rule. This model arrived AFTER the embedded seed snapshot (seed fetched 2026-08-12T10:07:29Z, model first observed 16:12:49Z), so it cannot be join-checked against the seed; post_seed records how its existence was verified instead.

cells.note: The catalog row is wrong twice over here, which is why this cell leads the batch: output equals context so it is a placeholder by the spec's rule, AND the real cap is 16x smaller. A consumer trusting the row reserves 1M against a 64k wall and gets an HTTP 400. NOT written as a provider-wide wildcard: the evidence names this model, and asserting it for all 20 ollama-cloud models would manufacture a claim from absence. If the cap is genuinely path-wide, one report naming a second model promotes it.

The clearest case for output.default existing as its own fact. models.dev publishes output=131072 for this model, and 131072 is the DEFAULT you get without asking — the cap is 1M, configurable. Some aggregators read the same 131k as the context window. One number, three wrong readings, and the split is what stops a consumer from inheriting any of them.

NO antigravity id minted: 1M input and 65k output on both the Antigravity and generateContent paths, so nothing has diverged. Antigravity's self-compaction around 135k is harness behaviour, not a window, and does not belong in this dataset. Separate geometry means a smaller output request buys no input headroom — the input_token_limit is the usable input, full stop.
